text:
sanjay: noticed some EU latency-alert pages didn't create PD incidents; paging dashboard shows spikes but PD shows fewer incidents. anyone seeing gaps?
rebecca: I saw repeated webhook failures from pagerbridge -> our suppressor then flagged a bunch as suppressed. looks like retries were misinterpreted. :grimacing:
mike: logs show a flurry at 12:02 UTC: upstream returned 503 on first attempts, then retries immediately. some of those retries created incidents, others were suppressed.
ops-bot: webhook-monitor: pagerbridge -> upstream 503 (x12 retries), queue length peaked 87
rebecca: quick check: the suppressor uses dedupe-key + TTL. after last deploy the TTL was cut from 60s -> 5s (PR-4849). if retries are spaced >5s they look new. but also we accidentally read `retry-count` as string in middleware and set `X-Pager-Suppress` when retry-count > '2' (string compare). so '10' < '2' lexicographically -> bug.
pagerbot: recent payloads: pl_a11, pl_a11, pl_a11, pl_b22, pl_b22, pl_c33, pl_c33, pl_d44
sanjay: that explains it. some retries treated as new -> caused duplicates -> other path suppressed later? messy. customer impact?
mike: two enterprise alerts for Dedicated EU didn't escalate to full PD rotation for ~8m. internal SLOs tripped, customers saw higher 95p latency but not outages. I'm manually re-notifying those PD incidents now.
oncall-manager: thanks for the heads up, please add affected tenants to the incident ticket so support can follow up.
rebecca: mitigation steps I'm doing now: 1) toggle header-based suppression OFF in config (kubectl -n infra patch cm pager-suppressor --patch '{"data":{"enable_header_suppress":"false"}}') 2) revert dedupe TTL to 60s (applying PR revert)
ops-bot: exec: patch configmap pager-suppressor -> success
ops-bot: exec: apply revert-pr-4849 -> success
sanjay: I'm restarting pagerbridge pods to clear the stuck retry queue: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/pagerbridge
ops-bot: rollout restart triggered; 3 pods -> terminating -> 3 running
mike: doing replay of webhook sequence to staging so we can validate dedupe logic under retries: `curl -sS -X POST https://staging.pagerbridge/_replay -d @test/retry-seq.json`
rebecca: note: PR-4860 fixes the retry-count parsing (cast to int) and removes the accidental string compare. merging to staging now.
rebecca: quick code snippet from buggy middleware for context:
```
// buggy
const retry = req.headers['retry-count'] || '0';
if (retry > '2') {
  req.headers['x-pager-suppress'] = 'true';
}
```
rebecca: fixed version casts to number before compare.
sanjay: timeline so far: 12:02 webhooks -> 503s and retries; 12:03-12:05 inconsistent dedupe TTL caused mixed creation/suppression; 12:10 manual mitigations applied; 12:12 pagerbridge restarted; 12:15 replays/tests in staging.
mike: created incident ticket I-2026 and added affected customers (tenant ids T-101,T-202). statuspage draft posted: "Degraded paging delivery due to retry + dedupe mismatch" (SP-790)
oncall-manager: please add followups: postmortem to include: 1) root cause (string compare + TTL change), 2) why retries were so bursty (upstream 503s), 3) improved test harness for replay under retry storms, 4) add unit test for header parsing.
rebecca: leaving a small smoke test in prod after deploy: send 3 rapid retries and confirm single PD incident created. will watch for 15m.
ops-bot: alert suppression metric back to normal range.
sanjay: thanks everyone. action items (assign): rebecca -> PR-4860 merge + prod deploy (in progress); mike -> confirm re-pages and notify oncall manager when complete; rebecca/mike -> run replay test and paste results here; eng-qa -> add regression test for dedupe TTL variants.
rebecca: replay results (staging): all 3 retries deduped correctly, single PD incident created.
mike: verified re-pages acknowledged by PD for both enterprise alerts. notifying customers in thread.
oncall-manager: marking incident as mitigated for paging delivery; please do a full postmortem writeup in incidents/postmortems within 48h. :thumbsup:
rebecca: filing postmortem draft PR-4950 now. includes root cause, timeline, remediation, and follow-ups.
sanjay: closing thread when postmortem linked. good catch on the lexicographical bug, that one is sneaky. :wave:
